description: Combined PRD evidence from two isolated Claude Code/Ralph stream worktrees. Verification and PR gate run on this integration branch.

userStories.title: User-role grant admin write rejects ambiguous JSON request bodies
userStories.description: POST /api/admin/users/{userId}/roles (UserRoleHandler.GrantRole at pkg/auth/user_role_handlers.go:116) still decodes its request body via json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&req). That decoder accepts only the first JSON value and silently drops any trailing bytes, so a concatenated payload like {"role":"viewer"}{"role":"admin"} hides intent from auditors and proxies. This endpoint actually mints role grants onto an existing user, so trailing-JSON smuggling is the same high-impact class that P2A-301..304 already closed for role definitions, group writes, service-account mutations, and API-key admin writes. Route GrantRole through httputil.ReadJSON so the single-JSON-value contract holds, and add a BDD integration test next to the handler asserting both the rejection and the existing happy path.
bddAcceptanceCriteria: Given POST /api/admin/users/{userId}/roles with a body of two concatenated JSON objects, when the handler decodes the request, then it returns 400 InvalidUserRoleRequest with a reason mentioning a single JSON value AND no role row is granted to the user.
Given POST /api/admin/users/{userId}/roles with a single well-formed body, when the handler runs, then the existing 200 OK happy path still persists the requested role.

A BDD integration test TestBDD_UserRoleGrantRejectsAmbiguousJSONBody_P2A305 lives in pkg/auth/user_role_handlers_bdd_test.go, reuses the shared assertSingleJSONValueRejection helper, and snapshots the user's role list before/after to prove the rejected request was non-mutating.

userStories.title: Save Dialog Warns on Duplicate Saved-Search Name
userStories.summary: The SavedSearchesPanel save dialog now detects a colliding name before POST (and as a fallback for stale-list 409 races) and surfaces an inline warning with the Save button disabled, replacing the unactionable `CONFLICT: SavedSearchNameConflict` error string.
